content:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple nodes reporting CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS / misaligned address errors on serving-runtime (inference-prod). Initial detections: gpu-12a, gpu-12b, gpu-9c. Error rate spike started ~2026-03-15T12:33:40Z. Paging SRE oncall. Severity: P1. Incident ticket INC-2026-045 created.

alex: Oncall (alex) here. Seeing increased 5xxs and OOM restarts for model-worker pods. Pulling nodes out of rotation now. Will try to scale up fallback capacity and route traffic to cpu-backed replicas.

alex: Quick check cmds I'm running:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n inference-prod -o wide | egrep "model-worker|fallback"
kubectl describe pod model-worker-rc-7f9 -n inference-prod
kubectl logs model-worker-rc-7f9 -n inference-prod --tail=200
nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR
sudo dmesg | tail -n 80 | egrep -i "CUDA|illegal|misalign|address"
```

jamie: grabbing logs now. I see repeated kernel trace lines showing misaligned address in cuda driver before container OOMs. Pasting relevant snippet.

jamie: ```
[Thu Mar 15 12:33:41.123] cuda: kernel: misaligned address 0x7fffa12b3c80 -> illegal memory access in ldm_execute
[Thu Mar 15 12:33:41.127] containerd: model-worker-rc-7f9 exited code=137 signal=0
[Thu Mar 15 12:33:41.130] kubelet: evicting pod model-worker-rc-7f9 due to OOM
[Thu Mar 15 12:33:41.131] nvidia: GPU-UUID 1234abcd: illegal memory access at 0x7fffa12b3c80
```

maya: eng-runtime chiming in. This looks like the misaligned-address/cuda_illegal_access pattern we've seen when a KV-cache race coincides with a specific kernel path on 525.x drivers. Two immediate mitigations: 1) disable pinned host memory / zero-copy for affected model workers, 2) switch routing to a safer quantized variant that doesn't use the problematic cache path. We have a hotpatch env var: RW_NV_SAFE_MODE=1 (toggles safer memory path) — can be rolled as config override to the node pool.

liam: SRE steps I'm executing:
- cordon gpu-12a, gpu-12b, gpu-9c
- drain with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-local-data, scale fallback replica set +4
- create temporary autoscaling override for inference-prod to prevent immediate downscales

liam: commands:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-12a && kubectl drain gpu-12a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference-prod &
kubectl scale rs/fallback-cpu-rs -n inference-prod --replicas=8
# patch daemonset to set RW_NV_SAFE_MODE=1 on next rollout
kubectl patch daemonset model-worker-ds -n inference-prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"RW_NV_SAFE_MODE","value":"1"}}]'
```

alex: I'm applying the patch to the model-worker daemonset now on a single node (canary) to watch for regressions before cluster-wide rollout. Doing a targeted rollout on gpu-9c first.

jamie: Observed one customer-facing error spike. cs-reported 12 requests failed for tenant_id=acme-staging between 12:33:40–12:36:00 with 502s. We should update status page.

customer-success: Draft status page blurb: "We are investigating elevated error rates for inference requests affecting a subset of GPU-backed nodes. Traffic is being routed to fallback CPU replicas while we mitigate. Some requests may see increased latency. No persistent data loss observed. Engineers are actively investigating." OK to post? :thinking:

alex: Post that. Also note impacted customers list: acme-staging, beta-api, finml-test. Add to incident ticket.

maya: Quick note about root causes to triage later: kernel-level race in NV driver + high concurrency on certain KV cache eviction path. If hotpatch works, followup action items: schedule driver upgrade sweep, add regression tests for KV cache concurrency, add runtime guard to detect misaligned access and fallback automatically.

liam: For now mitigation checklist (short):
- [x] cordon + drain affected nodes
- [x] scale fallback CPU replicas
- [x] enable RW_NV_SAFE_MODE on canary node
- [ ] monitor for additional illegal access traces for 30m
- [ ] if no regressions, rollout RW_NV_SAFE_MODE to rest of pool
- [ ] open driver-upgrade RFC / postmortem runbook

alex: Creating brief handoff note for next oncall (30m rotation):
- Current state: RW_NV_SAFE_MODE applied to gpu-9c (canary). Affected nodes cordoned. Traffic routed to CPU fallback. Error spikes reduced from ~12% to ~1.2% in the last 6m.
- Must monitor: dmesg/nvidia-smi for "illegal memory access"; application error rate; POD restart count.
- Links: INC-2026-045 (ticket), runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/serving/cuda-illegal-access (internal), logs query: https://logs.redwood.internal/q/INC-2026-045 (internal)

jamie: I'm attaching timeline to the incident ticket and will collect full dmesg traces + container core dumps for eng-runtime.

customer-success: Status page posted and customers notified via email template v3.0. Will update once we confirm cluster-wide rollout or driver patch.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager handoff scheduled in 30 minutes to oncall maya at 1768903034. Please acknowledge in thread when handing off.

alex: Acknowledged. Handoff ETA ~12:58Z. Leaving brief notes in the ticket.

maya: I see the canary metrics look stable so far. I'll take over the oncall after rotation and coordinate driver patch plan with eng-runtime if hotpatch proves stable.

liam: I'll keep an eye on autoscaling and routing. If error rate climbs >5% for 5 minutes, we revert to CPU-only routing and open broad mitigation.

jamie: uploading core dumps to s3://incidents/INC-2026-045/cores/ now.

alex: Thanks team. Will update thread if anything changes.
